long_biography.plain_text:
Stutterheim entered business through a courier company before joining Irfan van Ewijk and Theo Lelie to stage The Final Exam in 1992. The founders combined their own earnings with family loans and professional support, then turned the event into ID&T. Its growth across electronic music made Stutterheim a central figure in Dutch dance promotion and eventually led to the company's sale.

He redirected most of his proceeds into Amsterdam property, deliberately moving from dance events to buildings. As co-owner of the A'DAM Toren and Westergas site, and initiator of Makerstoren, he has focused on creative workspaces, cultural venues and mixed-use development. His continuing property activity, rather than his later Ajax board appointment, defines his principal commercial work.

uncertainties.detail: Ajax provides the exact public identity, birth details, career and current roles. The Spanish official gazette independently gives the full name Duncan Cornelis Patrick Stutterheim and joins him to TIKETITOO CHARTER SERVICE SL, whose name matches the selected vessel context. This is a high-specificity compound bridge, but the dossier does not infer that the company record itself proves personal vessel ownership.

Real Estate is used because Stutterheim directly said he redirected most SFX proceeds into property, current official material identifies major property co-ownership, and 2026 sources document continuing mixed-use development. His Ajax supervisory seat and residual ID&T advisory role are current secondary roles, not evidence that sport or entertainment remains his principal private commercial sector.

Founder accurately describes the historic ID&T wealth mechanism but the contract requires a current relationship. Stutterheim exited ID&T and now allocates capital to, co-owns and actively develops property. Investor therefore describes the present principal asset relationship, while the summary records his active project-initiation and development roles rather than reducing him to a passive holder.

The business was newly created and the founders supplied extensive labour and their own earnings, excluding inheritance. The record also shows material family advantage: an entrepreneur father whose business experience shaped Stutterheim, family financing and practical help, and professional support connected to the father's software company. Self-made — advantaged start is therefore more precise than either independent start or inherited wealth.

The middle names come from the official Spanish commercial gazette's exact identity bridge. Ajax supplies the exact birth date, Purmerend birthplace and repeated male identification; Wikipedia is used only to make the Netherlands birth-country statement explicit. No unsupported title, suffix or secondary nationality is proposed.

The dedicated Wikipedia page is authenticated against official Ajax, SEC and VPRO anchors. Makerstoren is proposed as a Company Website because its official page directly identifies and quotes Stutterheim as initiator and co-founder. Searches of LinkedIn, Instagram, Personal Website, Facebook, Twitter/X, YouTube and TikTok did not establish a collision-safe personal account with an official cross-link or two strong independent anchors.

Forbes has exact-person editorial coverage of Stutterheim's A'DAM Toren work and SFX's ID&T acquisition, but mandatory searches found no dedicated personal profile. The dossier therefore records not_found and does not propose a Forbes social.

Electronic dance music is assigned because Stutterheim's founder ownership and long operating mandate produced a recognised body of genre-defining event brands, not an incidental cultural association. Property developer is assigned for current repeated project-initiation and development work. Real estate investment management is excluded because the evidence does not establish management of third-party property capital, and inactive event-promotion and nightlife tags are not used.
